title: PHP 8.6 Released
excerpt: PHP 8.6 is a major update of the PHP language, with new features including Partial Function Application, a new Duration class, a Polling API, and a new clamp() function
content_html:
Released November 19, 2026

Faster, Safer, More Powerful.

PHP 8.6 is a major update of the PHP language, with new features including Partial Function Application, a new Duration class, a Polling API, and a new clamp() function

Key Features in PHP 8.6

More expressive code, stronger types, and scalable I/O.

Partial Function Application

Allows some of a function's arguments to be provided in advance, returning a Closure that accepts the rest.

New \Time\Duration Class

The Duration class represents elapsed time as measured by a stopwatch.

Polling API

Scalable I/O multiplexing using epoll, kqueue, and other native mechanisms, available to event loop libraries like ReactPHP and AMPHP.

New clamp() Function

Ensures that a given value (numeric or otherwise) falls within a specified range.

New SortDirection Enum

A standard, type-safe way to express sort order that can be shared across libraries.

Readonly Property Defaults

Allows readonly properties to declare default values, so fixed values no longer have to be assigned in the constructor.

Partial Function Application

Allows some of a function's arguments to be provided in advance, using ? and ... placeholders for the rest. The result is a Closure, and the function is only called once the remaining arguments are passed to it.

$versions = ['8.4', '8.5', '8.6', '8.7', '9.0'];

$supportsPfa = array_filter(
    $versions,
    fn ($version) => version_compare($version, '8.6', '>='),
);
$versions = ['8.4', '8.5', '8.6', '8.7', '9.0'];

$supportsPfa = array_filter(
    $versions,
    version_compare(?, '8.6', '>='),
);

New \Time\Duration Class

The Duration class represents elapsed time as measured by a stopwatch. Its representation is independent of any time and timezone and can represent a range of more than 250 years with nanosecond precision. This makes it well-suited to represent timeouts or benchmark timings in an expressive way.

/**
 * All delays are in microseconds.
 */
function backoff(
    int $baseDelay,
    int $step,
    int $attempt,
): void {
    $delay = $baseDelay + ($step * (2 ** $attempt));

    // Wait at most 30 seconds.
    usleep(min($delay, 30_000_000));
}

// 1 second base delay, plus 100 milliseconds
// doubling with each attempt.
backoff(1_000_000, 100_000, $attempt);
use Time\Duration;

function backoff(
    Duration $baseDelay,
    Duration $step,
    int $attempt,
): void {
    $delay = $baseDelay->add($step->multiplyBy(2 ** $attempt));

    // Durations are comparable, so min() works directly.
    $delay = min($delay, Duration::fromSeconds(30));

    time_nanosleep($delay->seconds, $delay->nanoseconds);
}

backoff(
    Duration::fromSeconds(1),
    Duration::fromMilliseconds(100),
    $attempt,
);

// Preconfigure the delays using Partial Function Application.
$waitBeforeRetry = backoff(
    Duration::fromSeconds(1),
    Duration::fromMilliseconds(100),
    attempt: ?,
);
$waitBeforeRetry($attempt);

Polling API

The new Io\Poll API efficiently monitors many streams at once using the best mechanism available on each platform (epoll, kqueue, event ports, or WSAPoll), without the scalability limits of stream_select(). It is designed as a common foundation that event loop libraries such as ReactPHP and AMPHP can build on.

$server = stream_socket_server('tcp://0.0.0.0:8080');
$clients = [];

while (true) {
    $read = [$server, ...$clients];
    $write = $except = null;

    // Based on select(), which typically can't handle
    // more than 1024 connections
    stream_select($read, $write, $except, null);

    foreach ($read as $stream) {
        if ($stream === $server) {
            $clients[] = stream_socket_accept($server);
            continue;
        }

        $data = fread($stream, 8192);

        if ($data === '' || $data === false) {
            $key = array_search($stream, $clients, true);
            unset($clients[$key]);
            fclose($stream);
        } else {
            fwrite($stream, $data);
        }
    }
}
use Io\Poll\{Context, Event};

$server = stream_socket_server('tcp://0.0.0.0:8080');

// Automatically uses epoll, kqueue, event ports, or WSAPoll
$poll = new Context();
$poll->add(new StreamPollHandle($server), [Event::Read]);

while (true) {
    foreach ($poll->wait() as $watcher) {
        $stream = $watcher->getHandle()->getStream();

        if ($stream === $server) {
            $client = stream_socket_accept($server);
            $poll->add(
                new StreamPollHandle($client),
                [Event::Read],
            );
            continue;
        }

        $data = fread($stream, 8192);

        if ($data === '' || $data === false) {
            $watcher->remove();
            fclose($stream);
        } else {
            fwrite($stream, $data);
        }
    }
}

Stream Error Handling

Stream operations can now be configured to throw a StreamException or to fail silently instead of emitting warnings. Errors are reported as structured StreamError objects with a StreamErrorCode enum case, the wrapper name, and the affected path or URL, and can also be retrieved later with stream_last_errors() or passed to a custom error handler.

$config = @file_get_contents('/etc/app/config.json');

if ($config === false) {
    // Only an unstructured message string is available
    $error = error_get_last();
    log_error($error['message']);
}
$context = stream_context_create([
    'stream' => [
        'error_mode' => StreamErrorMode::Exception,
    ],
]);

try {
    $config = file_get_contents(
        '/etc/app/config.json',
        context: $context,
    );
} catch (StreamException $e) {
    foreach ($e->getErrors() as $error) {
        // $error->code is a StreamErrorCode enum case
        log_error(
            $error->code->name,
            $error->message,
            $error->wrapperName,
        );
    }
}

New clamp() Function

Ensures that a given value (numeric or otherwise) falls within a specified range. Otherwise, the nearest boundary value is returned.

var_dump(max(0, min(-10, 100)));
// int(0)

var_dump(max(0, min(50, 100)));
// int(50)

var_dump(max(0, min(110, 100)));
// int(100)
var_dump(clamp(-10, 0, 100));
// int(0)

var_dump(clamp(50, 0, 100));
// int(50)

var_dump(clamp(110, 0, 100));
// int(100)

// Any comparable value works with clamp(). This
// includes the new Duration class.
var_dump(clamp(
    \Time\Duration::fromSeconds(30),
    min: \Time\Duration::fromMinutes(1),
    max: \Time\Duration::fromMinutes(10),
)->seconds);
// int(60)

New SortDirection Enum

The SortDirection enum provides a shared, type-safe way to express sort order with its Ascending and Descending cases. Previously, every library had to define its own way of representing sort direction, resulting in a mix of incompatible integers, strings, booleans, and custom enums. Since SortDirection is built into PHP, libraries can accept it in their public APIs without needing adapter code.

Learn more about this feature in The PHP Foundation’s blog.

class QueryBuilder
{
    private array $orderBy = [];

    public function orderBy(
        string $column,
        int $direction = SORT_ASC,
    ): static {
        $this->orderBy[] = $column . ' ' . match ($direction) {
            SORT_ASC => 'ASC',
            SORT_DESC => 'DESC',
        };

        return $this;
    }
}

$qb->orderBy('name', SORT_DESC);
$qb->orderBy('name', SORT_STRING);
// Accepted by the signature, then fails inside the method:
// UnhandledMatchError: Unhandled match case 2
class QueryBuilder
{
    private array $orderBy = [];

    public function orderBy(
        string $column,
        SortDirection $direction = SortDirection::Ascending,
    ): static {
        $this->orderBy[] = $column . ' ' . match ($direction) {
            SortDirection::Ascending => 'ASC',
            SortDirection::Descending => 'DESC',
        };

        return $this;
    }
}

$qb->orderBy('name', SortDirection::Descending);
$qb->orderBy('name', SORT_STRING);
// TypeError: QueryBuilder::orderBy(): Argument #2 ($direction)
// must be of type SortDirection, int given

Function and method parameters can now have their own DocComments, which are available via the new ReflectionParameter::getDocComment() method. This allows each parameter to be documented right next to its declaration, without repeating its name and type in a @param tag.

class DB
{
    /**
     * Returns up to $limit items matching the $query.
     *
     * @param string $query Terms to search
     * @param int $limit Maximum number of results
     */
    public function search(string $query, int $limit = 10): array
    {
        return [];
    }
}

// Parameter descriptions can only be extracted
// by parsing the function's DocComment.
class DB
{
    /**
     * Returns up to $limit items matching the $query.
     */
    public function search(
        /** Terms to search */
        string $query,

        /** Maximum number of results */
        int $limit = 10,
    ): array {
        return [];
    }
}

var_dump(
    new ReflectionParameter([DB::class, 'search'], 'query')
        ->getDocComment(),
);
// string(22) "/** Terms to search */"

New ReflectionProperty::isReadable() and ReflectionProperty::isWritable() Methods

With readonly properties, asymmetric visibility, and property hooks, checking whether a property is public is no longer enough to know whether it can be read or written. The new methods answer this directly for a given scope, and optionally for a specific object, taking into account visibility, initialization state, hooks, and magic methods.

class NewsEntry
{
    public string $title = 'PHP 8.6 released!';

    public private(set) string $slug = 'php-86-released';
}

$entry = new NewsEntry();
foreach (['title', 'slug'] as $item) {
    $property = new ReflectionProperty(NewsEntry::class, $item);
    printf(
        "%s: isReadable=%s isWritable=%s\n",
        $item,
        $property->isReadable(null, $entry) ? 'yes' : 'no',
        $property->isWritable(null, $entry) ? 'yes' : 'no',
    );
}
// title: isReadable=yes isWritable=yes
// slug: isReadable=yes isWritable=no

Readonly Property Defaults

Instance readonly properties, including those in readonly classes, can now declare a default value. This makes it simple to implement get-only interface properties with fixed values, which previously required assigning them in a constructor. The default counts as the property's initialization, so the constructor cannot overwrite it.

interface Rule
{
    public string $parser { get; }
}

final readonly class SlugRule implements Rule
{
    public string $parser;

    public function __construct()
    {
        $this->parser = SlugParser::class;
    }
}
interface Rule
{
    public string $parser { get; }
}

final readonly class SlugRule implements Rule
{
    public string $parser = SlugParser::class;
}

Additional Features and Improvements

  • The #[\Override] attribute can now be applied to class constants and enum cases.
  • Enums can now implement the __debugInfo() magic method.
  • Properties of objects stored in constants can now be modified directly, e.g. Config::DEFAULTS->timeout = 30.
  • New Uri\Rfc3986\UriBuilder and Uri\WhatWg\UrlBuilder classes build URIs from their components, along with new methods for detecting URI and host types and a Uri\WhatWg\url_percent_encode() function.
  • The Sodium extension adds post-quantum key encapsulation (X-Wing and ML-KEM-768), IP address encryption, and the SHAKE and TurboSHAKE extendable-output functions.
  • TLS streams now support session resumption, external pre-shared keys, and TLS 1.3 early data (0-RTT).
  • New mysqli::quote_string() method escapes a string and wraps it in quotes, matching PDO::quote().
  • pack() and unpack() now accept the < and > endianness modifiers on integer and float format codes.
  • JSON error messages now include the location of the error in the input.
  • The new error_include_args INI setting consistently includes function arguments in error messages.
  • New grapheme_strrev() function reverses strings by grapheme cluster, and the new IntlNumberRangeFormatter class formats ranges of numbers.
  • New ZipArchive::openString() and ZipArchive::closeString() methods work with in-memory archives.
  • Performance improvements include compiling array_map() with first-class callable or partial application callbacks into loops, faster printf() calls, caching of stateless closures, and faster JSON encoding.

Deprecations and Backward Compatibility Breaks

  • Using return inside a finally block is now deprecated, as it silently discards exceptions and overrides values returned from the try or catch block.
  • Returning a value from __construct() or __destruct() is now deprecated, as is making them generators. Declaring a nullable return type for __debugInfo() is also deprecated.
  • Using let or is as the name of a class, function, or constant is now deprecated. Using _ as a constant name, namespace as a class constant name, or readonly as a function name is also deprecated.
  • The mbstring regular expression functions such as mb_ereg() and mb_split() have been deprecated, as the underlying Oniguruma library is no longer maintained. PCRE functions with the u modifier can be used instead.
  • The is_double(), is_long(), is_integer(), and doubleval() aliases have been deprecated. Use is_float(), is_int(), and floatval() instead.
  • spl_object_hash() has been deprecated in favor of spl_object_id(), and spl_classes() in favor of ReflectionExtension::getClassNames().
  • Passing an object where an array is expected to array_walk(), array_walk_recursive(), http_build_query(), mb_convert_variables(), and compression functions and filters is now deprecated. Use get_object_vars() to convert the object first.
  • strcoll() and the SORT_LOCALE_STRING sort flag have been deprecated. Use the Collator class from the intl extension instead.
  • Passing a third argument to define() is now deprecated, as is calling is_a() or is_subclass_of() with a class name string when $allow_string is false.
  • Using more than 16 filters in a php://filter URL without setting the filter.max_filter_count context option is now deprecated.
  • Sessions are now more secure by default: session.use_strict_mode and session.cookie_httponly are enabled, and session.cookie_samesite is set to Lax.
  • Custom session handlers that do not implement both create_sid() and validateId() are now deprecated.
  • The metaphone(), mysqli_get_charset(), and mysqli_stmt_init() functions are now deprecated, along with the CSV methods of SplFileObject and the sorting, flag, and serialization methods of ArrayIterator.
  • trim(), ltrim(), and rtrim() now also strip form feed (\f) characters by default.
  • fclose(), file_put_contents(), and copy() now return false when flushing or closing the stream fails, instead of silently ignoring the failure.
  • Many functions now throw a ValueError for out-of-range values, invalid flags, or strings containing NUL bytes, instead of silently truncating or ignoring them.

blocks.html_en: New \Time\Duration Class

sentences.en: New \Time\Duration Class

blocks.html_en: The Duration class represents elapsed time as measured by a stopwatch. Its representation is independent of any time and timezone and can represent a range of more than 250 years with nanosecond precision. This makes it well-suited to represent timeouts or benchmark timings in an expressive way.

sentences.en: The Duration class represents elapsed time as measured by a stopwatch.
Its representation is independent of any time and timezone and can represent a range of more than 250 years with nanosecond precision.
This makes it well-suited to represent timeouts or benchmark timings in an expressive way.

blocks.html_en: Polling API

sentences.en: Polling API

blocks.html_en: The new Io\Poll API efficiently monitors many streams at once using the best mechanism available on each platform (epoll, kqueue, event ports, or WSAPoll), without the scalability limits of stream_select(). It is designed as a common foundation that event loop libraries such as ReactPHP and AMPHP can build on.

sentences.en: The new Io\Poll API efficiently monitors many streams at once using the best mechanism available on each platform (epoll, kqueue, event ports, or WSAPoll), without the scalability limits of stream_select().
It is designed as a common foundation that event loop libraries such as ReactPHP and AMPHP can build on.

blocks.html_en: Stream Error Handling

sentences.en: Stream Error Handling

blocks.html_en: Stream operations can now be configured to throw a StreamException or to fail silently instead of emitting warnings. Errors are reported as structured StreamError objects with a StreamErrorCode enum case, the wrapper name, and the affected path or URL, and can also be retrieved later with stream_last_errors() or passed to a custom error handler.

sentences.en: Stream operations can now be configured to throw a StreamException or to fail silently instead of emitting warnings.

Errors are reported as structured StreamError objects with a StreamErrorCode enum case, the wrapper name, and the affected path or URL, and can also be retrieved later with stream_last_errors() or passed to a custom error handler.

blocks.html_en: New SortDirection Enum

sentences.en: New SortDirection Enum

blocks.html_en: The SortDirection enum provides a shared, type-safe way to express sort order with its Ascending and Descending cases. Previously, every library had to define its own way of representing sort direction, resulting in a mix of incompatible integers, strings, booleans, and custom enums. Since SortDirection is built into PHP, libraries can accept it in their public APIs without needing adapter code.

sentences.en: The SortDirection enum provides a shared, type-safe way to express sort order with its Ascending and Descending cases.
Previously, every library had to define its own way of representing sort direction, resulting in a mix of incompatible integers, strings, booleans, and custom enums.
Since SortDirection is built into PHP, libraries can accept it in their public APIs without needing adapter code.

blocks.html_en: Function and method parameters can now have their own DocComments, which are available via the new ReflectionParameter::getDocComment() method. This allows each parameter to be documented right next to its declaration, without repeating its name and type in a @param tag.

blocks.html_en: New ReflectionProperty::isReadable() and ReflectionProperty::isWritable() Methods

sentences.en: New ReflectionProperty::isReadable() and ReflectionProperty::isWritable() Methods

blocks.html_en: With readonly properties, asymmetric visibility, and property hooks, checking whether a property is public is no longer enough to know whether it can be read or written. The new methods answer this directly for a given scope, and optionally for a specific object, taking into account visibility, initialization state, hooks, and magic methods.

sentences.en: With readonly properties, asymmetric visibility, and property hooks, checking whether a property is public is no longer enough to know whether it can be read or written.
The new methods answer this directly for a given scope, and optionally for a specific object, taking into account visibility, initialization state, hooks, and magic methods.

blocks.html_en: Readonly Property Defaults

sentences.en: Readonly Property Defaults

blocks.html_en: Instance readonly properties, including those in readonly classes, can now declare a default value. This makes it simple to implement get-only interface properties with fixed values, which previously required assigning them in a constructor. The default counts as the property's initialization, so the constructor cannot overwrite it.

sentences.en: Instance readonly properties, including those in readonly classes, can now declare a default value.
This makes it simple to implement get-only interface properties with fixed values, which previously required assigning them in a constructor.
The default counts as the property's initialization, so the constructor cannot overwrite it.

blocks.html_en: Additional Features and Improvements

sentences.en: Additional Features and Improvements

blocks.html_en: • The #[\Override] attribute can now be applied to class constants and enum cases.

sentences.en: The #[\Override] attribute can now be applied to class constants and enum cases.

blocks.html_en: • Enums can now implement the __debugInfo() magic method.

sentences.en: Enums can now implement the __debugInfo() magic method.

blocks.html_en: • Properties of objects stored in constants can now be modified directly, e.g. Config::DEFAULTS->timeout = 30.

sentences.en: Properties of objects stored in constants can now be modified directly, e.g. Config::DEFAULTS->timeout = 30.

blocks.html_en: • New Uri\Rfc3986\UriBuilder and Uri\WhatWg\UrlBuilder classes build URIs from their components, along with new methods for detecting URI and host types and a Uri\WhatWg\url_percent_encode() function.

sentences.en: New Uri\Rfc3986\UriBuilder and Uri\WhatWg\UrlBuilder classes build URIs from their components, along with new methods for detecting URI and host types and a Uri\WhatWg\url_percent_encode() function.

blocks.html_en: • The Sodium extension adds post-quantum key encapsulation (X-Wing and ML-KEM-768), IP address encryption, and the SHAKE and TurboSHAKE extendable-output functions.

sentences.en: The Sodium extension adds post-quantum key encapsulation (X-Wing and ML-KEM-768), IP address encryption, and the SHAKE and TurboSHAKE extendable-output functions.

blocks.html_en: • TLS streams now support session resumption, external pre-shared keys, and TLS 1.3 early data (0-RTT).

sentences.en: TLS streams now support session resumption, external pre-shared keys, and TLS 1.3 early data (0-RTT).

blocks.html_en: • New mysqli::quote_string() method escapes a string and wraps it in quotes, matching PDO::quote().

sentences.en: New mysqli::quote_string() method escapes a string and wraps it in quotes, matching PDO::quote().

blocks.html_en: • pack() and unpack() now accept the < and > endianness modifiers on integer and float format codes.

sentences.en: pack() and unpack() now accept the < and > endianness modifiers on integer and float format codes.

blocks.html_en: • JSON error messages now include the location of the error in the input.

sentences.en: JSON error messages now include the location of the error in the input.

blocks.html_en: • The new error_include_args INI setting consistently includes function arguments in error messages.

sentences.en: The new error_include_args INI setting consistently includes function arguments in error messages.

blocks.html_en: • New grapheme_strrev() function reverses strings by grapheme cluster, and the new IntlNumberRangeFormatter class formats ranges of numbers.

sentences.en: New grapheme_strrev() function reverses strings by grapheme cluster, and the new IntlNumberRangeFormatter class formats ranges of numbers.

blocks.html_en: • New ZipArchive::openString() and ZipArchive::closeString() methods work with in-memory archives.

sentences.en: New ZipArchive::openString() and ZipArchive::closeString() methods work with in-memory archives.

blocks.html_en: • Performance improvements include compiling array_map() with first-class callable or partial application callbacks into loops, faster printf() calls, caching of stateless closures, and faster JSON encoding.

sentences.en: Performance improvements include compiling array_map() with first-class callable or partial application callbacks into loops, faster printf() calls, caching of stateless closures, and faster JSON encoding.

blocks.html_en: Deprecations and Backward Compatibility Breaks

sentences.en: Deprecations and Backward Compatibility Breaks

blocks.html_en: • Using return inside a finally block is now deprecated, as it silently discards exceptions and overrides values returned from the try or catch block.

sentences.en: Using return inside a finally block is now deprecated, as it silently discards exceptions and overrides values returned from the try or catch block.

blocks.html_en: • Returning a value from __construct() or __destruct() is now deprecated, as is making them generators. Declaring a nullable return type for __debugInfo() is also deprecated.

sentences.en: Returning a value from __construct() or __destruct() is now deprecated, as is making them generators.
Declaring a nullable return type for __debugInfo() is also deprecated.

blocks.html_en: • Using let or is as the name of a class, function, or constant is now deprecated. Using _ as a constant name, namespace as a class constant name, or readonly as a function name is also deprecated.

sentences.en: Using let or is as the name of a class, function, or constant is now deprecated.
Using _ as a constant name, namespace as a class constant name, or readonly as a function name is also deprecated.

blocks.html_en: • The mbstring regular expression functions such as mb_ereg() and mb_split() have been deprecated, as the underlying Oniguruma library is no longer maintained. PCRE functions with the u modifier can be used instead.

sentences.en: The mbstring regular expression functions such as mb_ereg() and mb_split() have been deprecated, as the underlying Oniguruma library is no longer maintained.
PCRE functions with the u modifier can be used instead.

blocks.html_en: • The is_double(), is_long(), is_integer(), and doubleval() aliases have been deprecated. Use is_float(), is_int(), and floatval() instead.

sentences.en: The is_double(), is_long(), is_integer(), and doubleval() aliases have been deprecated.
Use is_float(), is_int(), and floatval() instead.

blocks.html_en: • spl_object_hash() has been deprecated in favor of spl_object_id(), and spl_classes() in favor of ReflectionExtension::getClassNames().

sentences.en: spl_object_hash() has been deprecated in favor of spl_object_id(), and spl_classes() in favor of ReflectionExtension::getClassNames().

blocks.html_en: • Passing an object where an array is expected to array_walk(), array_walk_recursive(), http_build_query(), mb_convert_variables(), and compression functions and filters is now deprecated. Use get_object_vars() to convert the object first.

sentences.en: Passing an object where an array is expected to array_walk(), array_walk_recursive(), http_build_query(), mb_convert_variables(), and compression functions and filters is now deprecated.
Use get_object_vars() to convert the object first.

blocks.html_en: • strcoll() and the SORT_LOCALE_STRING sort flag have been deprecated. Use the Collator class from the intl extension instead.

sentences.en: strcoll() and the SORT_LOCALE_STRING sort flag have been deprecated.
Use the Collator class from the intl extension instead.

blocks.html_en: • Passing a third argument to define() is now deprecated, as is calling is_a() or is_subclass_of() with a class name string when $allow_string is false.

sentences.en: Passing a third argument to define() is now deprecated, as is calling is_a() or is_subclass_of() with a class name string when $allow_string is false.

blocks.html_en: • Using more than 16 filters in a php://filter URL without setting the filter.max_filter_count context option is now deprecated.

sentences.en: Using more than 16 filters in a php://filter URL without setting the filter.max_filter_count context option is now deprecated.

blocks.html_en: • Sessions are now more secure by default: session.use_strict_mode and session.cookie_httponly are enabled, and session.cookie_samesite is set to Lax.

sentences.en: Sessions are now more secure by default: session.use_strict_mode and session.cookie_httponly are enabled, and session.cookie_samesite is set to Lax.

blocks.html_en: • Custom session handlers that do not implement both create_sid() and validateId() are now deprecated.

sentences.en: Custom session handlers that do not implement both create_sid() and validateId() are now deprecated.

blocks.html_en: • The metaphone(), mysqli_get_charset(), and mysqli_stmt_init() functions are now deprecated, along with the CSV methods of SplFileObject and the sorting, flag, and serialization methods of ArrayIterator.

sentences.en: The metaphone(), mysqli_get_charset(), and mysqli_stmt_init() functions are now deprecated, along with the CSV methods of SplFileObject and the sorting, flag, and serialization methods of ArrayIterator.

blocks.html_en: • trim(), ltrim(), and rtrim() now also strip form feed (\f) characters by default.

sentences.en: trim(), ltrim(), and rtrim() now also strip form feed (\f) characters by default.

blocks.html_en: • fclose(), file_put_contents(), and copy() now return false when flushing or closing the stream fails, instead of silently ignoring the failure.

sentences.en: fclose(), file_put_contents(), and copy() now return false when flushing or closing the stream fails, instead of silently ignoring the failure.

blocks.html_en: • Many functions now throw a ValueError for out-of-range values, invalid flags, or strings containing NUL bytes, instead of silently truncating or ignoring them.

sentences.en: Many functions now throw a ValueError for out-of-range values, invalid flags, or strings containing NUL bytes, instead of silently truncating or ignoring them.
